title: Linux - Interesting Files & Permissions (formerly Interesting Files & Permissions)
html:
Interesting Files and Permissions

File ownership, write access, mount options, and executable privileges can change a local user's effective reach. Begin by identifying the target file or execution path, then use the relevant page:

  • SUID, SGID, ACLs, and sensitive files gives a starting workflow for executable privileges and hidden access grants.
  • Arbitrary file write to root describes how writes to privileged paths can be turned into escalation.
  • Linux capabilities explains per-process and per-file capabilities.
  • SUID shared library and linker abuse covers dynamic loading around privileged binaries.
  • ld.so privilege escalation example follows a linker configuration case.
  • NFS no_root_squash and no_all_squash misconfiguration covers remote filesystem identity mapping.
  • Wildcard spare tricks covers argument expansion in privileged commands.
  • SELinux explains policy enforcement and relevant investigation steps.
